standard: Visible refinement acceptable at application scale; not a numerical quality score or release approval.

front.note: The small chair retains its wrapped back and four metal legs; the seat now has a quiet rounded rectangular crown.

rear.note: The curved back has continuous smooth surfaces and remains seated above the original leg frame.

detail.note: Full-size inspection shows continuous fine seat piping on the cover, without the previous floating corners or puckered edge.

underside.note: The original lower pan and four capped legs remain closed and connected; no additional underside openings appear.

clay.note: The neutral view confirms a coherent child chair silhouette. Its inherited thick cushion remains a stylized proportion, acceptable at application scale.

front.note: The rounded kettle lid and bowl form a continuous recognizable barbecue; the small damper is now fully visible on the dome.

rear.note: The smooth rear lid, handle and wheel frame retain their original layout without new surface intersections.

detail.note: Full-size inspection shows the damper seated to the curved lid rather than half buried. Four restrained dark vent marks remain legible; they are stylized solid marks.

underside.note: The lower bowl, ash cup, wheels and three supports remain readable and attached from beneath.

clay.note: The neutral silhouette shows the improved smooth spun shell with a closed rim and thin seated vent detail.

front.note: The full-size front view shows one continuous curved column from the bolted plinth to the shower head; the former section gaps are gone.

rear.note: The rear column has a continuous smooth bend and remains seated on its original base plate.

detail.note: The finish and original mixer and foot tap read clearly on the connected column; controls were preserved.

underside.note: The underside view retains the separate shower rose and base, with no visible breaks through the column.

clay.note: The neutral view confirms the original narrow shower proportions and a continuous crown. Its short upper bend remains intentionally compact.

front.note: The can retains its genuine open body and perforated rose; the new short neck visibly connects the rose to the original spout.

rear.note: The carrying and rear handles now have smooth rounded joints while retaining their original angular handle layout and attachments.

detail.note: Full-size inspection confirms the open rim, smooth handle sections and connected long spout. The metal grain remains stylized at close zoom.

underside.note: The closed can base and rose connection read continuously from below; the original perforation pattern remains intact.

clay.note: The neutral silhouette remains an immediately recognizable long-spout watering can with improved handle bends and no detached head.

front.note: Both low cross braces now meet the inclined side frames, while the original slatted seat and folding silhouette remain intact.

rear.note: The rear view shows the lower support aligned with both legs; original pivot and back rails remain readable.

detail.note: The seat slats, frame joints and painted steel retain clean edges with no new overlaps around the seating surface.

underside.note: Full-size underside inspection confirms both corrected braces connect to the frame on both sides; neither appears to float outside the legs.

clay.note: The neutral view confirms a coherent folding chair with unchanged stance and proportions and improved lower-frame construction.
